title: Checkpointed billing ledger for offline VPC collectors and reconciliation replays
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: On private/VPC and air-gapped deployments we receive usage events via on-prem collectors or offline export bundles. These events can arrive delayed, out-of-order, duplicated, or in larger batched chunks. Current hosted ingestion assumes near-real-time streams and does not handle long-delay reconciliation or retroactive quota enforcement. Goal: build a checkpointed, append-only billing ledger and replay pipeline that guarantees idempotent ingestion, supports delayed sync from air-gapped exports, and enables accurate retroactive accounting for quotas/rate-limits and billing. This ticket captures design and implementation for the ledger format, export manifest, replay idempotency, TTL/watermarking, and reconciliation jobs.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Offline export bundles produced by on-prem collectors include a signed manifest with monotonically increasing checkpoint ids and chunk checksums
A2: Ingestion pipeline supports replay of delayed bundles and applies events idempotently (no duplicate billing or quota crediting)
A3: Reconciliation job produces a daily ledger delta report that matches customer-side totals within 0.1% for last-30-day window
A4: Retroactive quota adjustments (e.g., enforce quota limits for past-period heavy use) can be flagged and applied without double-penalizing already-billed tokens
A5: All new artifacts have automated end-to-end tests and test vectors for out-of-order/delayed batches
A6: Documentation and console UI exports page updated with export schema and operator runbook
design_notes: Ledger: append-only, checkpointed segments. Each segment = compressed chunk with sequence range [start_seq, end_seq], segment_id, and SHA256 checksum. Segments are signed with deploy-specific key (customer-managed or Redwood key).
Manifest: JSON manifest at export root listing segments, checkpoint_id (monotonic), created_at, min_event_time, max_event_time, and optional resume_cursor for partial imports.

Idempotency: Each usage event includes (customer_id, local_instance_id, seq_num, event_hash). Ingestion will deduplicate by (customer_id, segment_id, seq_num) and maintain an ingestion cursor per customer that tracks last_applied_seq per local_instance_id.

Delayed sync: Support replay window configurable per-customer (default 90 days). Events older than retention are accepted for reconciliation but marked as 'out-of-window' for quota enforcement depending on customer policy.

Retroactive quota policy: two modes - 'soft-reconcile' (adjust internal accounting and billing only) and 'strict-enforce' (apply back-pressure penalties / quota changes retroactively). Strict mode requires explicit customer opt-in and reconciliation dry-run report.

Performance: ingestion will batch-apply segments; apply KV-cache protection to avoid blowing local rate-limit counters during replay: replay consumes tokens from a replay_budget that is separate from real-time quota counters to avoid denial during reconciliation runs.
Security: air-gapped bundle signed and optionally encrypted. Use keyed HMAC for signature verification when customer supplies shared key, otherwise Redwood signing keys are used with audit log entry.
implementation_steps: 1) Define and publish export manifest schema and segment format (spec + test vectors) - PR link in links
2) Extend on-prem collector to emit checkpoints and per-segment checksums (backfill existing collector versions where feasible)
3) Build ingestion microservice: segment verifier -> segment unpacker -> dedupe store lookup -> apply to ledger writer
4) Create ledger writer (append-only S3-backed + Postgres index) with checkpoint metadata and per-customer last-applied cursor
5) Implement reconciliation worker that computes deltas, produces reports, and optionally triggers billing adjustments
6) Add console UI for 'Offline exports' and reconciliation reports with links to runbook
7) Add end-to-end integration tests including compressed segment injection, out-of-order arrival, duplicate segments, and enclave-signed manifests
8) Rollout: feature-flag on private deployments, gradual enablement, and monitor metrics
test_plan: Unit tests for manifest parsing and signature verification (positive + negative cases)
Integration test: generate an export with 3 segments, shuffle order, import twice => importer should only apply once
Load test: replay 10M events across 1k customers, verify ingestion throughput and dedupe store scaling
Reconciliation test against golden ledger (simulate 7-day delay, then replay) and assert delta < 0.1%
Security test: verify encrypted bundle decryption and signature mismatch rejection
rollout_plan: Alpha: run in staging cluster with internal Private deployments and two pilot customers (opt-in)
Beta: enable feature-flag for all Private deployments with telemetry collection, do not auto-apply strict retroactive enforcement
GA: enable by default for new Private installs, provide migration tool for older collectors to generate manifests
Migration: provide CLI tool to create manifests from historical logs for customers who want full backfill
telemetry_and_metrics: alert: reconcile.delta > 1% over 24h for enterprise customers
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: replay could artificially exhaust runtime quotas if applied to live counters. Mitigation: separate replay_budget and dry-run mode; require explicit opt-in for strict retroactive enforcement.
Risk: malformed or tampered export bundles. Mitigation: require manifest signature verification and segment checksum validation; reject on mismatch and surface tamper report to operators.
Risk: large backfills create billing surprises for customers. Mitigation: reconciliation report with dry-run and hold for manual approval before billing adjustments.
Risk: dedupe store growth and index hot spots. Mitigation: use time-windowed sharded dedupe keys and TTLs; periodic compaction job to prune older cursors beyond retention window.
